claim: The chapter teaches that たい states only the speaker's own wish, is not for invitations, and is impolite in a 〜たいですか question to a superior, and no card in either unit says so.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1: "〜たい expresses the wish of the speaker and cannot be used to express the wish of anyone other than the speaker. か may be added ... but it is not appropriate for use when making an invitation. Also, it is considered impolite to use this expression when asking 〜たいですか ... especially to someone of higher status. ... it is safer to attach か to the ます-form of the verb (e.g., なにを のみますか)." Deck: seven question cards (where-eat-dinner どこでばんごはんをたべたいですか, aitai-3, ikitai-3, tabetakatta-3, mitakatta-3, ikitakunai-3, shourai-donna-tokoro-sumitai) and no note anywhere on the restriction.
fix: Add the caveat as a note on one or two of the たいですか cards (for example where-eat-dinner), saying たい is for your own wish and asking a superior 〜たいですか is rude; the ます-form + か is the safe question.

claim: Seven sentence notes say まえに always follows the dictionary form, which contradicts the chapter's own noun の まえに pattern.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "person は noun の まえに verb" and GRAMMAR 3: "verb 1 [dictionary form] まえに verb 2". Card notes: "まえに (mae ni, \"before\") always follows the dictionary form, as in ねるまえに from Lesson 17." on ikebana-wo-narau-mae-ni-hon, kuruma-wo-arau-mae-ni-hirugohan, shawaa-wo-abiru-mae-ni-kohii, kaigi-wo-hajimeru-mae-ni-kohii, toukyou-ni-sumu-mae-ni-uchi-wo-mitai, daunroodo-suru-mae-ni-mitai, meeru-wo-chekku-suru-mae-ni-asagohan. The same unit ships かいぎのまえに, パーティーのまえに and しごとのまえに.
fix: Reword to "after a verb, まえに follows the dictionary form" (a noun takes の, as in かいぎのまえに) on all seven cards.

claim: わたしはとうきょうにすみます does not mean "I live in Tokyo": non-past すみます means "will live" (going to live there), and the present state is すんでいます.
evidence: Book: すみます is glossed "live" and is used here only as すみたいです ("want to live"); the chapter never prints すみます as a present-state statement. Card: target わたしはとうきょうにすみます, English "I live in Tokyo."
fix: Change the sentence to a wish in this chapter's frame (e.g. とうきょうにすみたいです, "I want to live in Tokyo."), or re-gloss it as a future plan ("I will live in Tokyo.").

claim: The card puts の between a clock time and まえに and its note states this as a rule, but with a clock time Japanese says ごじまえに; the book's noun の まえに is for events and actions.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "noun の まえに verb ... Expresses what is/was done before the noun (event, action, etc.)"; every book example is an event (かいぎ, パーティー, ひるごはん). Card: ごじのまえにうちにかえりたいです, note: "A time word takes の (no) before まえに (mae ni): ごじのまえに (go-ji no mae ni), like かいぎのまえに."
fix: Replace the time with an event (e.g. ばんごはんのまえにうちにかえりたいです) and drop the "time word takes の" claim from the note.

claim: The sentence uses みてください, and みて (the て-form of みます) has never been taught; the deck only has fixed chunks such as みせてください and きてください.
evidence: Ledger before Lesson 17 holds ちょっとまってください, おしえてください, みせてください, まってください and きてください, but no みて. Card (aiSuggested): このえいがはぜひみてください, "Please be sure to see this movie."
fix: Rebuild with a taught form, e.g. このえいがはぜひみたいです ("I definitely want to see this movie."), or drop the card; zehi-1 already covers ぜひ + きてください.
